findings.title: The opening name is identified through the surah
findings.claim: The basmala places Allah's distinctive name at its center. Luqman later identifies that same name as the answer to who created the heavens and earth, says that what is in the heavens and earth belongs to Allah, and shows people calling on Allah when waves cover them. The opening name thus leads into both recognition of God's lordship and enacted reliance on Him.
findings.mechanism: The focus's definite proper name Allah is the named carrier. At 31:25 it is the answer to the question of who created the heavens and earth, and 31:26 places the heavens and earth under Allah. The surah then prohibits associating partners with Allah, directs submission to Him, and uses the same proper name as the object of a direct call in 31:32. These separate creation, devotion, and appeal relations bring the proper-name and worship branches into contact without changing the focus phrase's form.
findings.reader_payoff: The name at the threshold is tied to the surah's own account of the Creator, the one owed exclusive devotion, and the one called on in danger.
findings.containment: The basmala remains a naming phrase. The later creation answer, submission, and storm call are contextual echoes; they do not turn the opening into a creation statement, an oath, or a plea.

epistemic.reason: The cited host-surah passages state creation, exclusive submission, and calling directly, while joining them as a reading of the opening name is a contextual inference. The proper-name branch is itself marked qualified in the supplied lexicon, and the packet supplies no separate source-trust labels.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: Yaratıcıya özgü ad ile seslenme ve ant biçimleri
branch_activations.facet_statement: Dalın merkezinde, Yaratıcıyı başkalarından ayırarak gösteren ve yalnız ona özgü sayılan özel ad bulunur.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's definite divine proper name Allah, governed within the opening phrase 'in the name of' and anchoring the mercy epithets.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: At 31:25 the reply to who created the heavens and earth is Allah; at 31:26 the heavens and earth are said to belong to Allah.
branch_activations.activation: The named Creator and owner in the host-surah context is the referent of the same proper name at the opening, so the opening name points into the surah's account of Allah's lordship.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The Allah named at the threshold is heard as the Creator and owner whom the surah later acknowledges.
branch_activations.boundary: This contextual identification does not expand the basmala's grammar into a statement about creation or ownership.

branch_activations.branch_gloss: Yaratıcıya özgü ad ile seslenme ve ant biçimleri
branch_activations.facet_statement: Özel adın doğrudan ya da seslenme öğesi yerine geçen bir sonla kullanılması, yakarma ve dilek bildiren seslenme biçimleri kurar.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's definite proper name Allah remains the name at the center of the opening phrase.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: When waves cover them, people call on Allah and devote their religion sincerely to Him in 31:32.
branch_activations.activation: The context's explicit call uses the same distinctive proper name carried by the focus, bringing the branch's invocation use into a relation with the opening name.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening name is connected to the name the surah's people directly call on when danger overwhelms them.
branch_activations.boundary: The later call keeps its own storm setting; it does not make the basmala itself a plea.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Temel eylem, bir varlığa tapınmak ve kişinin kendini bu tapınmaya vermesidir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus carries Allah as a definite proper name; the name itself does not spell out an act of worship.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: Luqman's counsel rejects associating partners, 31:22 describes submitting one's face to Allah, and 31:32 depicts callers devoting religion sincerely to Him.
branch_activations.activation: The surah's separate acts of exclusive submission and devotion establish the worship relation around the referent named at the focus.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening proper name is placed in the host surah's field of exclusive devotion to Allah.
branch_activations.boundary: This preserves the focus's proper-name form and does not claim that the name lexically means the act of worship.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Eylemden türeyen varlık anlamı, kendisine tapınılan varlığı veya tapınma konusu sayılan nesneyi gösterir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus is a proper-name occurrence of Allah, not a generic noun for a deity.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The context prohibits associating anything with Allah, directs submission to Allah, and names Allah as the object of the storm-time call.
branch_activations.activation: Those relations show that the proper name's referent is also the one toward whom worship and supplication are directed; the form restriction does not exclude that contextual referential role.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: Alongside its unique proper-name role, Allah is the named referent whom the surah treats as the object of exclusive devotion and appeal.
branch_activations.boundary: The context supports this role for the referent without converting the proper name into a generic lexical label for every worshiped entity.

findings.title: Mercy with a life-carrying contour
findings.claim: The opening's Rahman and Rahim remain names of divine mercy. The surah soon speaks of guidance and mercy for those who do good, then places the same root beside a mother's carrying and its closing mention of the wombs. That root echo lets the opening mercy be heard alongside care that carries life, while its ordinary meaning remains intact.
findings.mechanism: The two focus adjectives carry the mercy branch and are attached to Allah. Luqman 31:3 repeats mercy as a benefit for the doers of good; 31:14 depicts a mother carrying her child through weakness, and 31:34 uses the same root in the noun for wombs. The explicit womb occurrence and maternal carrying scene contact the focus's mercy through the shared root and bodily image, allowing a qualified life-bearing resonance.
findings.reader_payoff: Divine mercy remains the primary reading but can be perceived beside the surah's concrete picture of life carried and sustained.
findings.containment: The adjectival forms do not mean 'womb,' and the basmala does not state that mercy is specific to pregnancy or motherhood. The maternal and womb scenes remain contextual images that enrich, rather than replace, the opening's ordinary mercy meaning.

epistemic.reason: The packet supplies accepted mercy and womb branches, an explicit same-root womb occurrence, and a maternal carrying scene. Applying the noun's bodily branch to the focus's adjectival mercy forms is a contextual resonance rather than a lexical synonymy, and the packet supplies no separate source-trust labels.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Bu iç yöneliş, acınan kişiyi esirgemeyi ve ona iyilikte bulunmayı gerektiren etkin bir sonuç taşır.
branch_activations.carrier: The two definite adjectives attached to Allah carry the branch's mercy meaning, with the focus's primary reading remaining divine mercy.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The surah's early description names guidance and mercy for the muhsinin, giving mercy a stated recipient in 31:3.
branch_activations.activation: The same mercy term returns in the host surah as something reaching those who do good, relating the opening's divine mercy to a stated benefit within the surah.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening mercy is contextualized as mercy that reaches the surah's doers of good alongside guidance.
branch_activations.boundary: 31:3 does not define the adjectives or limit divine mercy to the stated recipients.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Tanrı hakkında kullanıldığında esirgemenin genişliği ve yaratılmışlara iyilik olarak ulaşması belirginleşir.
branch_activations.carrier: The epithets are divine mercy predicates in apposition to Allah, so the branch's stated God-specific use applies at the focus.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: At 31:3 the host surah places mercy alongside guidance and directs it to those who do good.
branch_activations.activation: The context gives the divine mercy named at the opening an explicit recipient and benefit within the surah's opening description.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The divine mercy at the opening is heard as reaching the surah's good-doers through the guidance it describes.
branch_activations.boundary: The context does not claim that the book is the only means or recipient of divine mercy.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Dişi bedenindeki bu iç organ, yavrunun oluşup geliştiği yer ve onu karın içinde taşıyan kap işlevindedir.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus's adjectives carry mercy, not the noun for womb; both nonetheless arise under the supplied r-h-m root record.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: At 31:34 the noun al-arham names wombs under the same root, while 31:14 says that a mother carried her child through weakness.
branch_activations.activation: The literal womb occurrence and the separate maternal carrying scene contact the focus's mercy through a shared root and life-bearing image, making the womb branch available as a qualified contextual resonance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The opening's mercy can be heard alongside an image of life-bearing, protective care within the surah.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus adjectives do not literally mean womb, and the bodily image does not define or restrict divine mercy.
